sources.entry: Shark - Cursor IDE workspace manager for macOS.

summary.one_liner: A native macOS app (SharkSpace) that organizes project and component folders into virtual workspaces built from real directories and symlinks, so Codex, Claude Code, terminals and other agent tools can open them like ordinary projects.
summary.what_it_does: Shark creates a real directory for each workspace and mounts multiple project or component folders into it via symlinks, with metadata stored in .shark-workspace.json. It provides a sidebar of workspaces (pin, rename, health check with symlink rebuild) and a folder list showing git branch, latest tag, working tree and upstream status, plus a workspace-wide Git overview. It also lists Codex sessions for each workspace, with activity grouping, archiving, deletion, display names, preview, and jumping to running iTerm2 sessions after installing Codex hooks. The README also describes a Venomfiles dependency checker and a component selector that browses configurable search paths.
use_cases: group several repositories into one folder for an AI coding agent
open a multi-repo workspace in a terminal or editor with one double-click
browse and resume Codex sessions per project on macOS
check workspace folders for missing or broken symlinks
view git status across many repositories at once
how_to_run: Alternatively, download the latest SharkSpace-x.x.x.dmg from Releases, open it, and drag SharkSpace.app to Applications
If macOS reports "Shark is damaged", run: xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/SharkSpace.app
Clone the repository: git clone (URL not given in README), cd Shark, ./install_latest.sh
notable: Virtual workspaces are real directories containing symlinks, so any tool that opens a folder can open the whole workspace
Local-first: metadata stays on the machine, with no telemetry or cloud sync
Codex session browser with activity groups, archive handling, previews and iTerm2 jump via installed hooks
Non-destructive project handling: removing or renaming a project only changes Shark's list, not the directory on disk
caveats: Sparkle auto-update is marked as in development; 1.14.0 lacks it, and unsigned (no-certificate) builds are not notarized and may need manual approval in macOS privacy settings
Some features depend on Codex hooks, iTerm2, or Venomfiles, which must be set up separately
keywords: open multiple folders in one place
